title: Sixteen-board deployment CFR breadth scale
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: At fixed approximate solver compute and identical conservative distillation, increasing deployment-matched SRP+3BP board diversity from four deep i200 boards to sixteen i50 boards will improve unseen-board and live Slumbot generalization more than additional per-board CFR iterations.
material_change: Solve sixteen deterministic diverse 200bb deployment-grid boards for SRP and 3BP at b8/i50, convert with the validated compact bridge, train H64 source-KL1 L2=.01 adapters with board-disjoint splits, and gate on heldout KL, 10k mirror, then fresh Slumbot.

code.provenance_gap: Historical record predates automatic patch/source-manifest capture; the exact dirty worktree cannot be reconstructed post hoc.

notes: Post-hoc infrastructure repair refreshed verifiable wall-time and artifact-integrity fields. The exact historical dirty-worktree patch/source manifest and placeholder commands cannot be reconstructed without falsifying provenance; the record explicitly preserves that gap.

result.summary: Sixteen-board b8/i50 breadth produced 1.62M validated compact rows and strong heldout teacher fit, but all three adapter epochs were negative in the same 4096-pair mirror test (about -0.70 to -1.54 bb/100).
result.conclusion: At this resolution, adding board breadth degrades internal play relative to the four-board i200 adapter. The prior measured i50-to-i200 strategy drift makes shallow teacher bias the leading explanation; no candidate is promoted to Slumbot.
result.next_step: Build an eight-board b8/i200 teacher by reusing the four completed deep boards and solving four new diverse boards, then repeat the identical H64 conservative adapter gate. This isolates resolution from breadth without re-solving existing work.
